parsed.explanation: The border itself is the primary universal exposure: appearance is compared against passport sex at the main gateways, and in 2025 two trans women were X-rayed to verify genital anatomy, mocked, refused entry and had passports seized, with refusals documented from 2016 through 2025. Beyond the border, gender nonconformity is a criminal offence (Art. 412(2), up to a year; predecessor Art. 359 punished clothing inappropriate to one's sex in any circumstances), enforced on presentation: visitors were sentenced to a year (2017) and held three months (2013), with head-shaving, discarded hormone pills and forced rectal examinations documented in custody, and one trans foreigner held unresolved since 2022. No anti-discrimination law, no legal recognition, no functioning advocacy or remedy. Only the absence of a capital provision and the recent shift toward detention-and-deport rather than imprisonment keep this above the execution-tier anchors.

entry_documents.exposure: Routine comparison of appearance with passport sex at the main airports; 2025 X-ray genital verification, staff mockery, refused entry and passport confiscation; refusals 2016, 2022, 2025; a 2025 transit refusal.
entry_documents.protection: Not documented. No sourced rule recognises corrected markers or bars anatomy-based screening.
entry_documents.interaction: Border officers' discretion feeds directly into hours-long detention and exclusion; whether a corrected marker changes outcome is unsourced.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: 2017: three weeks in a cell for 'effeminate detainees', heads shaved, hormone pills discarded, one-year sentence later commuted to deportation; 2013: ~3 months' detention, fine, deportation; trans foreigner held since Sept 2022, release unrecorded; beatings and forced rectal examinations documented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: None documented; 2017 defendants had no legal representation; consulate accused of negligence (2023).
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Presentation-based charge converts into custody placement by appearance, where medication and dignity are removed; deportation follows.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Custody in a ward designated for effeminate detainees; Art. 412(2) criminalises a man disguising himself to enter women-only space, but records show charges for appearance in ordinary mixed-gender places; local public-morals offences operate alongside federal code.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No facility-access or placement protection for trans visitors.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Emirate-level morality offences layer on the federal offence, widening exposure beyond the border.

care_services.exposure: Hormone pills discarded in detention (2017); state surgery severely restricted; conversion practices lawful; no health protection on gender identity.
care_services.interaction: Care interruption compounds custody harm; no clinical recourse for a detained visitor.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Gender nonconformity criminalised; enforcement turns on presentation; officials publicly hostile; trans content censored; no LGBTQI+ organisation may register or operate.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Legal threat-framing legitimises police and public action against visibly gender-nonconforming visitors.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented for travelling minors or guardians.
minors_guardians.interaction: Not documented; guardianship concepts noted in the dossier are resident-facing only.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 2011 police campaign targeting transsexuals and masculine-presenting women; 2013 visitors who reported prejudice were themselves detained; 2020 arrests of foreign residents over clothing.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Not documented; reporting invites detention rather than help.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Calling police converts a victim into a suspect, removing any street-level recourse.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination law, no legal gender recognition, no registrable advocacy body, no documented successful complaint by a trans visitor.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Not documented. Oversight or appeal mechanisms reaching visitors are absent from the record.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Without remedy, entry refusal and custody outcomes are effectively final; frequency of refusals is unquantified.

anchor_checks.comparison: That anchor has a capital provision, routine arrest, months of pretrial custody, beatings and compelled confessions. Here there is no capital clause and the presentation offence caps at one year, but the dossier adds universal border anatomy screening and documented visitor imprisonment with head-shaving and pill confiscation. Similar severe tier, marginally above.

Vellandra excludes trans visitors with no arrest or charge. This dossier is materially worse: exclusion is accompanied by genital X-ray verification, a live criminal offence enforced on presentation, documented one-year sentences and abusive custody, so it sits well below that anchor.

Kestrel Isles imposes administrative refusal after discretionary secondary screening. Here the outcome includes anatomical verification, passport seizure, prosecution and detention harm, placing the jurisdiction far below that friction-only tier.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime combines an inescapable, degrading border screen keyed to appearance against passport sex with a live criminal offence covering gender presentation and a documented record of visitor prosecutions and abusive detention. The state, not private actors, is the perpetrator at every stage: screening, arrest, custody placement, medication confiscation. No anti-discrimination law, no legal recognition, no registrable advocacy and a record of police turning reports against trans complainants leave no working remedy. Recent practice trends toward detention-then-deportation rather than imprisonment, and the absence of any capital provision keeps the jurisdiction above the execution tier, but a trans visitor outed at the border faces near-certain exclusion and a credible route to prosecution and harmful custody.
